Ok, first, this should NEVER be a crime. I've been on a train with people sleeping on two or three seats, or keeping their bags or precious shopping goods on a seat, but if it bothers me, it is my responsibility as a self-righteous human being to tell the person and ask them to move. 99% of the time they will move.

However, I'm a fan of Malcolm Gladwell. In his book, the "Tipping Point," he talks about "broken windows" style policing, and it has brought down overall crime rates. Things like cleaner streets reduce crime. In Gladwell's book, he says that cracking down on people hopping the turnstiles to get onto the subway for free reduced overall crime. As much as I'd love a free train ride, I'm sure my couple bucks doesn't begin to cover the cost of my ride, so I accept paying it. If others don't, well, there are consequences, and science has showed us that making them face these consequences reduces more serious crimes, like murder or robbery.

But I agree with the commenters who say this is often used as an excuse to arrest minorities. The idea is good, but the reality we live in is quite dark.
